clues: A 38-year-old woman has months of episodic headaches and palpitations that her clinic has attributed to anxiety.
Her blood pressure is 190/110 and drops markedly on standing; spells are triggered by abdominal pressure or certain medications.
A random glucose is elevated and CT shows a 4 cm heterogeneous adrenal mass with high attenuation before contrast.
Plasma free metanephrines are more than four times the upper limit of normal.
cases.teaching: Start alpha blockade before beta blockade to avoid unopposed alpha stimulation and a hypertensive crisis.

clues: A 45-year-old man has hypertension that remains uncontrolled despite three antihypertensive drugs including a diuretic.
He reports muscle weakness and cramps; sodium is 144 mEq/L and serum bicarbonate is mildly elevated.
Potassium is 3.0 mEq/L with inappropriate urinary potassium wasting, and a 1.5 cm adrenal nodule is seen on CT.
Plasma aldosterone to renin ratio is markedly elevated with a suppressed renin level.
cases.teaching: Screen for primary aldosteronism in resistant hypertension, hypokalemia, or an adrenal incidentaloma using the aldosterone to renin ratio.

clues: A 32-year-old woman has several days of fatigue, headache, and a low-grade fever.
She is confused and mildly jaundiced; creatinine is 1.6 mg/dL and platelets are 12,000/uL.
Hemoglobin is 7.8 g/dL with elevated LDH and indirect bilirubin, a negative Coombs test, and normal PT and aPTT.
The peripheral smear shows numerous schistocytes and ADAMTS13 activity is below 10 percent.
cases.teaching: Start plasma exchange emergently when a pentad-like picture with schistocytes and thrombocytopenia appears; do not wait for ADAMTS13 results and avoid platelet transfusion.

clues: A 52-year-old woman has months of fatigue, weight loss, and nausea with vague abdominal pain.
She is lightheaded on standing and her blood pressure is 88/54; sodium is 126 mEq/L and potassium is 5.6 mEq/L.
Her skin is darkened in the palmar creases and buccal mucosa, and she has mild hypoglycemia and eosinophilia.
Morning cortisol is low with a high ACTH and a flat response to cosyntropin stimulation.
cases.teaching: Hyperpigmentation plus hyperkalemia suggests primary adrenal failure; give stress-dose steroids before the diagnosis is confirmed in crisis.

clues: A 27-year-old woman has repeated emergency visits for severe abdominal pain with a normal examination and normal imaging.
The pain began a week before her menses after a crash diet; she also has constipation and a heart rate of 120.
She develops proximal weakness, seizures, and a sodium of 124 mEq/L, and her urine darkens after standing in sunlight.
Urine porphobilinogen is markedly elevated during an attack.
cases.teaching: Treat acute attacks with IV hemin and glucose, and review the drug list to remove porphyrinogenic agents.
cases.review_notes: Some may answer just 'porphyria' which is intentionally allowed as an alias.

clues: A 19-year-old college student has two months of unexplained fatigue and mildly elevated aminotransferases.
Over the same time his handwriting worsened and he developed a tremor and slurred speech.
Alkaline phosphatase is surprisingly low relative to bilirubin, and he has a Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia.
Slit-lamp examination shows Kayser-Fleischer rings and ceruloplasmin is low.
cases.teaching: Test for Wilson disease in anyone under 40 with unexplained liver disease, especially with psychiatric or movement symptoms.

clues: A 26-year-old woman has several months of low-grade fevers, fatigue, and weight loss.
She notices left arm fatigue with use and has lightheadedness when turning her head quickly.
Blood pressure is 150/90 in the right arm and 96/60 in the left arm, with a subclavian bruit and elevated ESR.
CT angiography shows long smooth stenoses of the aortic arch branches with wall thickening.
cases.teaching: Suspect Takayasu in a young woman with absent pulses or a blood pressure discrepancy between arms.

clues: A 66-year-old man has several months of fatigue and back pain that worsens at night.
Hemoglobin is 9.1 g/dL, creatinine is 2.3 mg/dL, and total protein is high with a low anion gap.
Calcium is 12.1 mg/dL and a rouleaux formation is seen on the smear; urine dipstick is negative for protein.
Serum protein electrophoresis shows an M spike and bone marrow biopsy has 40 percent clonal plasma cells with lytic skull lesions.
cases.teaching: A negative urine dipstick with heavy proteinuria suggests Bence Jones light chains, which dipsticks do not detect.

clues: A 34-year-old Black woman has a persistent dry cough and fatigue for several months.
She has tender red shins and ankle swelling, and her calcium is mildly high.
Chest radiograph shows bilateral hilar enlargement and the ACE level is elevated.
Biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas, and cultures and stains for organisms are negative.
cases.teaching: Sarcoid is a diagnosis of exclusion that requires non-caseating granulomas and exclusion of infection and other causes.

clues: A 41-year-old man has two weeks of fever above 39 C that has not responded to broad antibiotics.
He now has splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and rising liver enzymes with a falling fibrinogen.
Ferritin is 28,000 ng/mL and triglycerides are markedly elevated.
Bone marrow shows macrophages engulfing blood cells and soluble IL-2 receptor is very high.
cases.teaching: Very high ferritin with fever and cytopenias should prompt HScore calculation, and a search for the trigger such as infection or lymphoma.

clues: A 29-year-old woman is brought in after a fall; her partner says she has had weight loss for months.
Temperature is 39.8 C, heart rate is 150 and irregular, and she is agitated and tremulous.
Examination shows a diffuse goiter, lid lag, and warm moist skin; she recently had an infection and stopped her medicines.
TSH is undetectable with markedly elevated free T4 and a Burch-Wartofsky score above 45.
cases.teaching: Treat thyroid storm with a thionamide first, iodine an hour later, a beta blocker, and steroids.

clues: A 68-year-old woman with diabetes has two hours of nausea, fatigue, and a sense of indigestion that is not relieved by antacids.
She is diaphoretic and short of breath, and her vital signs show mild hypotension.
ECG shows ST elevation in the inferior leads with reciprocal changes in aVL.
Troponin is rising and angiography shows an occluded right coronary artery.
cases.teaching: Women, older adults, and patients with diabetes often present with atypical symptoms, so get an ECG early.
cases.review_notes: Aliases like 'ACS' and 'STEMI' are accepted for simplicity.

clues: A 55-year-old man has had three days of new fatigue and a brief fainting spell while climbing stairs.
He recently returned from a long flight and now has pleuritic chest pain with a heart rate of 112.
The oxygen saturation is 90 percent on room air with a clear chest radiograph and a swollen left calf.
CT pulmonary angiography shows a filling defect in the right pulmonary artery.
cases.teaching: Syncope with a clear chest film and hypoxia should raise PE high on the differential, and the right ventricle should be assessed.

clues: A 22-year-old man has two days of vomiting and abdominal pain and was told he has a stomach virus.
He is breathing deeply and quickly with dry mucous membranes and a heart rate of 118.
Glucose is 520 mg/dL with an anion gap of 28 and a pH of 7.1.
Serum and urine ketones are strongly positive, and he has no known diabetes history.
cases.teaching: Replace fluids first, then give insulin only once potassium is above 3.3 mEq/L, and look for the precipitant.

clues: A 47-year-old man has had two weeks of fatigue, night sweats, and low back pain.
He has a new heart murmur and painless red spots on the palms, and his hemoglobin is 10 g/dL.
He has splinter hemorrhages and painful nodules on his finger pads, and an IV drug use history.
Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus in four of four bottles and echo shows a mobile valve vegetation.
cases.teaching: Obtain at least three sets of blood cultures before antibiotics when endocarditis is suspected, and apply the Duke criteria.

clues: A 72-year-old woman has a new headache, fatigue, and a low-grade fever for several weeks.
She has aching in her shoulders and hips and pain when she chews food.
ESR is 94 mm/h, and she describes a brief loss of vision in one eye yesterday.
Temporal artery biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells.
cases.teaching: Start high-dose glucocorticoids immediately when GCA is suspected with visual symptoms, before the biopsy.

clues: A 61-year-old woman has progressive fatigue and a feeling that her memory has slipped over the past year.
She has constipation, weight gain, a hoarse voice, and cold intolerance, and her LDL cholesterol is newly elevated.
Examination shows dry skin, delayed relaxation of ankle reflexes, and a heart rate of 52.
TSH is 78 mIU/L with a low free T4, and anti-TPO antibodies are positive.
cases.teaching: Check TSH in patients with cognitive decline, hyperlipidemia, or unexplained fatigue.

clues: A 35-year-old woman has long-standing iron deficiency that has not improved despite oral supplements.
She also has mild osteopenia, intermittent bloating, and recurrent mouth ulcers.
She has an itchy blistering rash on her elbows and knees, and her aminotransferases are mildly elevated.
Anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA is strongly positive and duodenal biopsy shows villous atrophy.
cases.teaching: Refractory iron deficiency without a bleeding source warrants celiac testing, and the patient must be on gluten when tested.

clues: A 58-year-old man with uncontrolled hypertension has abrupt severe pain that began in his chest and moves to his back.
The pain is maximal at onset and he describes it as tearing; blood pressure differs by 30 mmHg between his arms.
He has a new diastolic murmur, and a chest radiograph shows a widened mediastinum.
CT angiography demonstrates an intimal flap in the ascending aorta.
cases.teaching: Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis when dissection is possible, and control heart rate before blood pressure.

clues: A 44-year-old woman reports the worst headache of her life that peaked within a minute while she was exercising.
She vomited twice and has a stiff neck and sensitivity to light but no focal weakness.
Her blood pressure is 176/98 and a non-contrast head CT is performed six hours after onset.
CT shows blood in the basal cisterns and angiography identifies a posterior communicating artery aneurysm.
cases.teaching: Non-contrast CT within six hours of onset is nearly 100 percent sensitive; nimodipine reduces delayed ischemia.

clues: A 24-year-old man who smokes has had a week of cough, fatigue, and dark tea-colored urine after a recent viral illness.
He coughs up small amounts of blood, and his hemoglobin has fallen to 8.5 g/dL with iron deficiency pattern.
Creatinine rises from 1.0 to 4.5 mg/dL over days; urine shows dysmorphic red cells and red cell casts, and chest imaging shows alveolar opacities.
Serum anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies are positive and kidney biopsy shows linear IgG staining.
cases.teaching: Treat anti-GBM disease urgently with plasma exchange, cyclophosphamide, and steroids, and advise the patient to stop smoking.
cases.review_notes: Linear IgG is on immunofluorescence; clue wording could be tightened.

clues: A 55-year-old man was admitted yesterday and started treatment for a bulky lymphoma with a very high white count.
Overnight he has nausea, muscle cramps, and reduced urine output.
Creatinine rose from 1.1 to 3.4 mg/dL and phosphorus is 8.2 mg/dL with a low calcium.
Uric acid and potassium are markedly elevated, and the ECG shows peaked T waves.
cases.teaching: Prevent tumor lysis syndrome with aggressive hydration and allopurinol or rasburicase before cytotoxic therapy in high-risk disease.

clues: A 34-year-old woman with a BMI of 14 is admitted for severe malnutrition and started on enteral feeding.
On the third day she is weak and short of breath, and she develops swelling in both legs.
Phosphorus is 0.9 mg/dL, with low potassium and magnesium, and her heart rate is irregular.
Insulin surge from carbohydrate feeding drove electrolytes into the cells, and thiamine was not given before feeds.
cases.teaching: Give thiamine before feeding and replace phosphate, potassium, and magnesium while advancing calories slowly in malnourished patients.

clues: A 69-year-old man who smokes has two weeks of nausea, headache, and mild confusion.
He is euvolemic on examination, and his sodium is 121 mEq/L with a serum osmolality of 252 mOsm/kg.
Urine osmolality is 480 mOsm/kg and urine sodium is 55 mEq/L with a low uric acid.
Chest imaging shows a central lung mass and biopsy reveals small cell carcinoma.
cases.teaching: SIADH is a diagnosis of exclusion that requires euvolemia and normal thyroid, adrenal, and renal function.

clues: A 58-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis has had rising abdominal girth for months.
After a large paracentesis he becomes oliguric, and his creatinine rises from 1.2 to 3.0 mg/dL.
Urinary sodium is under 10 mEq/L, the sediment is bland, and creatinine does not improve after 48 hours of diuretic withdrawal and albumin.
There is no shock, nephrotoxin exposure, or structural kidney disease on ultrasound.
cases.teaching: Hepatorenal syndrome is functional renal failure from splanchnic vasodilation; treat with albumin plus terlipressin or norepinephrine.

clues: A 63-year-old woman is in the ICU with gram-negative sepsis from a urinary source.
New oozing is noted from her IV sites, and her platelet count has fallen from 210,000 to 38,000/uL.
PT and aPTT are both prolonged, and fibrinogen is 70 mg/dL.
D-dimer is very high and the smear shows schistocytes.
cases.teaching: Treat the underlying cause of DIC; replace products only for bleeding or procedures.

clues: A 70-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease has a day of vomiting and weakness.
She is breathing rapidly, with a blood pressure of 100/60 and normal oxygen saturation.
The creatinine is 4.1 mg/dL and she takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily.
Arterial pH is 7.05 with an anion gap of 30, lactate of 14 mmol/L, and no ketones.
cases.teaching: Metformin is contraindicated at an eGFR under 30 mL/min, and severe cases may need hemodialysis.
cases.review_notes: Answer 'metformin toxicity' is not in alias list; faculty may want to add it.

clues: A 58-year-old man has several months of fatigue, joint pain, and a rash that worsens in cold weather.
He has palpable purpura on the legs and a peripheral neuropathy with numb feet.
Urine shows blood and protein, and C4 is very low with a positive rheumatoid factor.
Serum precipitates when cooled, and he tests positive for hepatitis C antibody.
cases.teaching: Warm the blood sample to the lab; hepatitis C is the leading cause of mixed cryoglobulinemia.

clues: A 30-year-old woman has had three first-trimester pregnancy losses.
She develops a deep vein thrombosis in the left leg without any provoking factors.
She has a lacy reticular rash on her legs, and aPTT is prolonged and does not correct with mixing.
Anticardiolipin and anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies are positive on two occasions twelve weeks apart.
cases.teaching: Warfarin is preferred over direct oral anticoagulants in high-risk, triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome.

clues: A 40-year-old woman has gained weight over a year, particularly in her face and abdomen, with new easy bruising.
She has resistant hypertension, new diabetes, and menstrual irregularity.
Examination shows violaceous abdominal striae, a dorsocervical fat pad, and proximal muscle weakness.
A 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test fails to suppress cortisol and a late-night salivary cortisol is elevated.
cases.teaching: Confirm hypercortisolism with biochemical testing first, then use ACTH to localize the source.

clues: A 36-year-old man on a long-term antidepressant is given a new medicine for migraine and a cough suppressant.
Within hours he is agitated and sweating, with diarrhea and a temperature of 38.9 C.
He has inducible clonus in both ankles, hyperreflexia, and dilated pupils.
Symptoms improve after stopping the drugs and treatment with benzodiazepines and cyproheptadine.
cases.teaching: Clonus and hyperreflexia with rapid onset after serotonergic drugs distinguish serotonin syndrome from NMS, which has rigidity and slow onset.

clues: A 64-year-old man on long-term simvastatin was started on clarithromycin for pneumonia a week ago.
He now has severe muscle aches and weakness in both thighs and notes dark urine.
Urine dipstick is strongly positive for blood but there are few red cells on microscopy, and creatinine is 3.2 mg/dL.
Creatine kinase is 48,000 U/L with high potassium and phosphorus.
cases.teaching: CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin raise simvastatin levels; treat with aggressive IV fluids.

clues: A 28-year-old woman started a new anticonvulsant four weeks ago and now has fever and a sore throat.
She develops painful oral and conjunctival erosions and dusky target-like lesions on her trunk.
Skin detaches with gentle lateral pressure, with 8 percent of body surface area involved.
Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal necrosis with minimal inflammation, and the culprit is lamotrigine.
cases.teaching: Stop the offending drug immediately; the SCORTEN score predicts mortality and care is best in a burn unit.
cases.review_notes: SJS and TEN differ by BSA; the clue 8 percent BSA is SJS-TEN overlap by some definitions, review.

clues: A 31-year-old man with schizophrenia was started on a high dose of haloperidol injections three days ago.
He is now agitated, sweaty, and has a fever of 40.1 C with a heart rate of 128.
His muscles feel stiff like a lead pipe and he has fluctuating blood pressure.
Creatine kinase is 12,000 U/L and he has leukocytosis, with normal reflexes and no clonus.
cases.teaching: Stop the antipsychotic and give supportive cooling and fluids; dantrolene or bromocriptine are options in severe cases.

clues: A 62-year-old man is on day 7 after a knee replacement and receiving heparin prophylaxis.
His platelet count falls from 240,000 to 90,000/uL, a drop of more than 50 percent.
He develops a new swollen leg and a pulmonary embolus despite therapeutic heparin.
The 4T score is high and platelet factor 4 antibodies are strongly positive.
cases.teaching: Stop all heparin, including flushes, and start a non-heparin anticoagulant such as argatroban when HIT is suspected.

clues: A 78-year-old woman with heart failure and atrial fibrillation has had days of nausea, anorexia, and fatigue.
A new loop diuretic and an antibiotic were recently added, and she reports blurry yellow-tinted vision.
Potassium is 3.1 mEq/L, creatinine is higher than baseline, and the ECG shows scooped ST segments.
Telemetry shows atrial tachycardia with block and bidirectional ventricular tachycardia.
cases.teaching: Hypokalemia and renal impairment worsen digoxin toxicity, and digoxin-specific antibody fragments are the antidote.
cases.review_notes: Chronic toxicity often has near-normal levels; review wording.

clues: A 55-year-old woman with bipolar disorder takes a stable dose of lithium and begins a new medicine for knee pain.
She develops coarse tremor, nausea, and diarrhea, then slurred speech and unsteady gait.
Creatinine is mildly increased, and she has recently been on an ACE inhibitor and an NSAID.
Serum lithium level is 3.2 mEq/L and hemodialysis is recommended.
cases.teaching: NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, and thiazides reduce lithium clearance and can precipitate toxicity.

clues: A 24-year-old woman is brought in after a fight with her partner and vomiting; she denies ingestion.
She had mild nausea for a day, and her initial examination is unremarkable.
Two days later she has right upper quadrant pain, an INR of 3.4, and ALT above 5,000 U/L.
A four-hour serum level plotted on the nomogram was in the treatment range, and N-acetylcysteine is started.
cases.teaching: Start N-acetylcysteine early; the benefit is greatest within eight hours of ingestion.

clues: A 30-year-old man develops shortness of breath and bluish discoloration after a dental procedure.
His saturation reads 85 percent and does not rise with high flow oxygen, and he is not distressed.
His blood looks chocolate brown, and the arterial partial pressure of oxygen is normal.
Co-oximetry shows methemoglobin of 35 percent after benzocaine spray, and methylene blue is given.
cases.teaching: Pulse oximetry trends toward 85 percent in methemoglobinemia; methylene blue is ineffective in G6PD deficiency.

clues: A 72-year-old man with diabetes starts trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary infection while taking lisinopril and spironolactone.
He becomes weak and has palpitations five days later.
His creatinine is 2.4 mg/dL and the ECG shows peaked T waves and a widened QRS.
Serum potassium is 7.4 mEq/L and he receives IV calcium gluconate.
cases.teaching: Trimethoprim blocks the epithelial sodium channel like amiloride, so combining it with ACE inhibitors and spironolactone can cause severe hyperkalemia.

clues: A 40-year-old man has tingling in both feet that began ten days after a diarrheal illness.
Over three days he develops weakness that ascends from his legs to his thighs and hands.
Reflexes are absent in the legs, and his forced vital capacity is declining at the bedside.
Cerebrospinal fluid shows elevated protein with normal cell count, and nerve conduction demonstrates demyelination.
cases.teaching: Monitor forced vital capacity and negative inspiratory force, and treat with IVIG or plasma exchange.

clues: A 48-year-old man has fatigue, joint pain, and reduced libido for several years.
He has pain and swelling in the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints, and new diabetes.
His skin has a gray bronze tint, and ferritin is 2,800 ng/mL with transferrin saturation over 80 percent.
HFE genotype testing shows C282Y homozygosity, and treatment with phlebotomy is planned.
cases.teaching: Screen with transferrin saturation and ferritin; phlebotomy prevents cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

clues: A 62-year-old man who smokes has fever and a dry cough that started after a hotel stay.
He has watery diarrhea and confusion, and his sodium is 128 mEq/L with a high bilirubin.
Chest radiograph shows a patchy lobar infiltrate that progresses despite beta-lactam therapy.
Urinary Legionella antigen is positive and he improves on azithromycin.
cases.teaching: Atypical pneumonia with hyponatremia, diarrhea, and travel history should prompt urinary antigen testing.

clues: A 63-year-old man who smokes has progressive leg weakness and difficulty rising from a chair.
He has a dry mouth and erectile dysfunction, and his reflexes are diminished.
Strength improves briefly after repeated effort and he has no ptosis early in the disease.
Repetitive nerve stimulation shows an incremental response, with antibodies against voltage-gated calcium channels and a small cell lung mass.
cases.teaching: Always search for small cell lung cancer when Lambert-Eaton is diagnosed in a smoker.
